answer: Persistent Behavioural Fingerprint Rule: each identity commits a hash of its full interaction history from epoch to epoch; a new identity whose history fails to match any prior trace is admitted only at a low trust tier. Enforcement compares the fable of past actions against current conduct, so a sybil farm must replicate consistent behaviour across many epochs. Attackers pay sustained compute and latency to build believable timber of activity. This trellis of linked epochs makes each fresh identity cost weeks of coherent, non-repeating behaviour before it earns weight,
